podaccess:item.itunes:title: Andrew Ng on the delusion of AI doom
podaccess:item.itunes:summary:
Will AI destroy humanity? Amid doom-laden debates on the trajectory of the technology, our guest has a refreshingly optimistic perspective. Andrew Ng is the co-founder of Google Brain and one of the architects of modern AI. Unlike many of the other AI heavyweights, however, he doesn’t think the technology poses the existential threat to humans that everyone else is warning about. What makes him so positive?


Guests and hosts:

  • Alex Hern, AI writer at The Economist
  • Andrew Ng, co-founder of Google Brain, Coursera and LearnVector
  • Alok Jha, The Economist’s science and technology editor


Watch Alex’s full interview with Andrew Ng on The Economist’s “Inside Tech”.


Topics covered:

  • AI existential risk
  • AI jobs apocalypse
  • Artificial general intelligence


Transcripts of our podcasts are available via economist.com/podcasts.


Listen to what matters most, from global politics and business to science and technology—subscribe to The Economist.

podaccess:item.itunes:title: The 2026 Nobel prizes for science
podaccess:item.itunes:summary:
Six more scientists have joined the esteemed ranks of Nobel laureates this week. Their work spanned optogenetics, neutrino detection and mirror-image molecules. How will their discoveries change the world?


Guests and hosts:

  • Geoff Carr, senior editor for science and technology at The Economist
  • Sam Wikeley, The Economist’s science correspondent
  • Nikita Ostrovsky, science and tech writer at The Economist
  • Alok Jha, The Economist’s science and technology editor


Topics covered:

  • Optogenetics
  • Neutrino astronomy
  • Life’s asymmetry


For more, listen to our September 2025 episode, “JUNO: the hunt for the universe’s most elusive particles”.


Transcripts of our podcasts are available via economist.com/podcasts.


Listen to what matters most, from global politics and business to science and technology—subscribe to The Economist.

item.title: Trailer: Tocqueville Road Trip
item.itunes:title: Trailer: Tocqueville Road Trip
item.itunes:subtitle: Democracy in America at 250
item.description:
When Alexis de Tocqueville visited America from France in 1831 he saw a new kind of society. Not just a country, but an idea that would change the world. His book “Democracy in America” was a big influence on later generations of writers and thinkers, including The Economist’s US Editor John Prideaux. Now, 250 years after its birth, the vitality of that democracy is under question. In this series, John retraces the route Tocqueville took to find out how much of what inspired Tocqueville about America remains—and how worried we should be about what’s changed.


Out now


Find the show on The Economist app | On Spotify | On other apps
